comments.body:
Root-cause investigation (2026-11-03, dev host, load average about 30-38, worktree at origin/main).

The idle time is not a sleep, polling interval, lock timeout, or subprocess grace period. It is git process startup cost on this host, multiplied by the number of git processes each test starts.

Observations:
- cProfile of test_server_never_pushes_and_workspace_is_isolated: 43.6 s of 54.4 s is select.poll inside subprocess.communicate, across 124 child processes. No time.sleep or lock wait appears.
- GIT_TRACE2_EVENT over the same test: the 120 top-level git processes report about 4.5 s of git-internal runtime in total.
- 25 runs of `/opt/homebrew/bin/git --version` from Python: 5.89 s wall vs 0.31 s git-internal. About 95% of each git call is spent before git's main or after it exits.
- Exec median from Python: Homebrew git 0.11-0.33 s (max 1.3 s); /usr/bin/true 0.016 s; jq 0.016-0.018 s; plutil (also links CoreFoundation) 0.031 s. So the delay is specific to starting git on this host; CoreFoundation linkage alone does not explain it.
- Spawns per test, measured: the test-side `_make_source` (git init + rebar.init_repo + create_ticket) starts about 52 processes (10-15 s); `jobs.run_job` starts 34-60 (7-14 s). Example: test_completion_pass_binds_server_derived_values = 112 spawns, 29.1 s.

Consequence: a test-only change (build the authoritative source once per module, which the no-push assertions leave untouched) removes about 52 spawns per test, roughly 45% of the wall time. Estimated module total falls from about 310 s to about 170 s at this load. That does not meet the "under 120 s" AC; reaching it requires fewer git processes inside run_job (production: opcert_service workspace prepare + init ensures), or a faster git exec on the host.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py::test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir` runs `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py` and `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity.py` in a nested pytest. On the loaded macOS dev host the nested run took 318-360 s, over the 300 s per-test budget in `pyproject.toml`, so the outer test failed with a pytest-timeout (under xdist: a crashed worker). CI passes.

## Root cause (measured; detail in the 2026-11-03 comment)

No sleep, poll interval, lock timeout, or grace period. The idle time is git process startup on this host (about 95% of each git call happens outside git's own runtime; median exec 0.11-0.33 s versus 0.016 s for `/usr/bin/true`), multiplied by the git processes each test starts: about 52 in the test-side `_make_source` (git init, `rebar.init_repo`, `rebar.create_ticket`) and 34-60 inside `jobs.run_job`.

## Approach

Build the authoritative source once per module instead of once per test. Every test in the 2 modules uses it read-only: `jobs.run_job` clones it into a discarded workspace and never pushes (the no-push tests assert exactly that), so one shared instance per module is sound. Replace `_make_source(tmp_path, monkeypatch)` with a module-scoped fixture built under `tmp_path_factory`, with `REBAR_ROOT` set through a `pytest.MonkeyPatch.context()` only while building. The fixture's teardown asserts every ref of the shared source is unchanged, so a test that mutated it fails loudly instead of leaking state. No `cp -R` (a copied `.tickets-tracker` shares the original gitdir). No autouse fixtures; the per-test budget is not raised.

Cutting the git processes inside `jobs.run_job` is production code and is split into a separate follow-up bug (linked `discovered_from`).

## Scope

- `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py`: module-scoped `authority` fixture replaces per-test `_make_source`.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity.py`: same.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py`: new test that runs nested `pytest --setup-plan` (no test bodies execute) on each module, through `_nested_pytest.run_nested_pytest` with `_subprocess_env.subprocess_env`, and asserts the authoritative source is set up once at module scope.

## Testing

- New `--setup-plan` test fails before the change (no module-scoped source) and passes after.
- Existing tests in both modules pass unchanged in their assertions, including the no-push byte-identity checks.
- Edge: the fixture teardown ref-snapshot check fails if any test writes to the shared source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The blocking call behind the ~28 s per-test time is identified and recorded on this ticket (git process startup cost times per-test git process count; see the 2026-11-03 comment).
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity.py` (with `-p no:xdist`) finishes under 300 s on the dev host; the wall time and the load average at the time are recorded on this ticket, before and after.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py` passes on the dev host, with the new `--setup-plan` test included.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0 with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.
- [x] A follow-up bug for reducing the git process count inside `jobs.run_job` is filed with the measured numbers and linked `discovered_from` this ticket.
